transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CardioNest CTO), Marcus Lee (CardioNest ML Eng), Helen Ortiz (CardioNest Platform), Tom Baker (CardioNest SRE)

Summary:
Brief retro on last week's TTFT/streaming experiments, review of microburst results, discuss kernel routing decisions and sequence-length hedging, finalize next steps for bandwidth/first-token targets, and confirm security gating items for pilot expansion.

Topics covered:
- TTFT variance and microburst causes
- Streaming vs. batch tradeoffs for CardioNest interactive searches
- Sequence-length distribution impact on kernel selection
- Fallback strategies (dedicated vs hosted; model variants)
- Security: KMS, audit logs, data residency questions

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya Chen: okay, great, everyone there? thanks for hopping on. agenda is quick retro on the numbers from the stream test and then decide kernel pathing.
00:12 Priya Rao: yep, we can start. we had a few late high-priority items so appreciate the time.
00:20 Liam O'Neill: quick note up front - we ran two microburst windows on Wednesday, one with continuous batching at 50ms, one with the hedging enabled. saw a decent drop in tail but some variance around the 95th.
00:35 Marcus Lee: yeah, the 95th improved by about 18% in the hedged run, but we saw some jitter at 99.9 that was surprising. the jitter lines up with ~3% of requests that are seqlen > 1024.
00:50 Tom Baker: those are the long transcripts - user transcripts from device-uploads. they spike length and the runtime is sensitive.
01:05 Sofia Alvarez: when you say jitter, the traces show extra context-switching? I saw a few K-V cache misses that added ~120ms.
01:18 Marcus Lee: the transcriber called it K V cash in the logs actually, so there's some noise in naming but it's definitely the KV cache thrash.
01:30 Maya Chen: classic. for the pilot we can do a two-pronged approach: selective quantized kernels for normal seqlen and a full-precision path for long seqlen, plus an early-resp stream cutoff for interactive queries.
01:45 Priya Rao: cost is a big concern - if we go multi-path are we looking at doubling GPU counts? need the economics.
02:00 Maya Chen: not doubling, but there is an increase. we'll provide a delta table. important to note dedicated instances let you pin QoS so latency SLOs are easier; hosted will be cheaper initially but more variable.
02:18 Helen Ortiz: also curious about encryption - we need to ensure HSM/KMS integration for key management. is Redwood Private ready?
02:30 Liam O'Neill: yes, Private supports KMS and can be deployed in your VPC; audit logs can be exported. we do want to run the security follow-up; SOC2 is in place, but we'll walk through the specifics of retention windows.
02:48 Priya Rao: retention and data residency - we have EU users and want EU-only storage.
02:55 Maya Chen: noted - we'll flag region pinning for the pilot.
03:05 Marcus Lee: back to the benchmarks - can you walk us through the 50ms batching run and why the 99.9 spikes remain?
03:18 Liam O'Neill: Sure - at 50ms the runtime will batch when requests arrive; most of your traffic falls into sub-200-token which batches well. the 99.9 spikes correlate to the long tail seqlen events which cause KV cache growth and force kernel fallback.
03:35 Marcus Lee: is there an option to stream partial tokens earlier? for our product the first token latency matters more than full completion.
03:48 Sofia Alvarez: streaming early tokens is possible - we can return a preliminary chunk from the fast int8 path then stitch with the F32 path for the remainder. there will be some complexity in ensuring consistency but it greatly reduces TTFT.
04:06 Tom Baker: any accuracy regressions with int8 stitching? we can't have hallucinations in the medical context.
04:18 Liam O'Neill: good question - for our tests on the model variant we saw less than 0.8% regression on the eval set; but because you have clinical prompts we recommend running your eval shards.
04:33 Priya Rao: we'll need to run those evals. Marcus can do that.
04:40 Marcus Lee: yep, will run shard with 10k prompts. estimated 48 hours.
04:48 Maya Chen: excellent. another lever is sequence-length hedging: detect long input early (token 8-16) and route to full-precision path, otherwise favor quantized fast kernels. hedging reduces jitter but can increase nominal cost.
05:05 Priya Rao: what's the heuristic threshold you'd recommend? 256? 512?
05:12 Liam O'Neill: starting point 512. your histogram suggests ~7% above 512. switching at 512 got us best latency/cost tradeoff in our sims.
05:25 Helen Ortiz: operationally how do we switch kernels without downtime?
05:32 Sofia Alvarez: runtime supports live kernel swaps per-request. the trick is warm caches - we pre-warm common KV prefixes for the heuristics and keep a small dedicated hotset on the same node.
05:45 Tom Baker: that pre-warming - is it manual or automatic?
05:50 Liam O'Neill: can be automatic - we have a warmup policy that observes prefix frequency and warms on a schedule. we'll send the config we used.
06:05 Maya Chen: ok so action items - Liam will run a controlled microburst with beam variance toggles and share traces; Marcus will give us the seqlen distribution.
06:18 Priya Rao: timeline - if all go well we'll expand pilot to staging in two weeks.
06:25 Maya Chen: noted - we should aim for staging by 12/13.
06:30 Marcus Lee: quick security note - CardioNest needs exact PII flow doc for the SRE team.
06:36 Maya Chen: will include data-flow and encryption notes in the security follow-up.
06:45 Priya Rao: competitors? we ran a quick bench with Vertex and saw a similar drop with their auto-batching but it cost more. Anthropic had fewer tail spikes but limited streaming support.
06:58 Maya Chen: good color, thanks. one more operational ask: can Redwood capture token-level latency traces and export as CSV?
07:05 Liam O'Neill: yes, we can export per-token latencies and a flamegraph of kernel selections.
07:12 Tom Baker: great, that'll help root cause.
07:20 Sofia Alvarez: we'll include a short playbook on fallback rules: primary fast-int8, hedged full-fp for long seqlen, fallback to smaller batch non-hedged if GPU saturates.
07:34 Marcus Lee: any gotchas on model variants? we've got a fine-tuned model with a slightly different tokenizer.
07:42 Liam O'Neill: tokenizers can cause slight seqlen diffs; we recommend normalizing before routing - we'll add a step to the playbook.
07:55 Priya Rao: ok, recap and owners?
08:00 Maya Chen: recap - microburst benchmark run 11/30 (Liam), seqlen export 11/29 (Marcus), pricing delta by 12/01 (Maya), kernel swap playbook 12/02 (Sofia), security follow-up 12/03 (Maya + Security).
08:23 Priya Rao: sounds good. thanks all.
08:30 Maya Chen: thanks team, we'll follow up in email with links to the traces and the draft playbook.
08:38 Meeting end.
